name: roboto-to-lerobot
description: Converts Roboto ingested data referenced by a Roboto Collection of events or of sessions into a LeRobot dataset, one output episode per event or per session in the collection. Which topics become which state, action, and video features is driven entirely by a contract YAML read from the invocation dataset (defaults to 'contract.yaml' at the dataset root) — see https://docs.roboto.ai/reference/roboto-to-lerobot-contract.html for the contract schema and https://docs.roboto.ai/user-guides/convert-to-lerobot.html for the authoring guide. Deployed as two variants with an identical interface: roboto-to-lerobot-v2_1 writes LeRobot 2.1 datasets (lerobot 0.3.3) and roboto-to-lerobot-v3_0 writes LeRobot 3.0 datasets (lerobot 0.7.0); only v3_0 supports sharded (parallel) writing, except with the episode cache, which converts episodes in parallel on both.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: ID of a Roboto Collection whose resource_type is 'event' or 'session'. Each event or session in the collection becomes one episode in the output LeRobot dataset: an event covers its time window on its first associated dataset, a session covers its time window on its own files.

parameters.name: output_tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated tags to add to the output dataset once the converted files are uploaded, for example to start a trigger on dataset.tag_added. Requires the invocation's output dataset to be set. Unset, the runtime uploads the output after the action exits and nothing is tagged.

parameters.name: subtask_events
parameters.description: Which events on a session become its episode's sub-tasks, by event name: comma-separated glob patterns, where a leading '!' excludes. An event is used when it matches one of the patterns without '!' (or when there are none) and none of the patterns with '!'. For example 'grasp*,lift' uses only those events and '!qa/*' uses every event except those under 'qa/'. Unset, every event becomes a sub-task. Applies to collections of sessions on roboto-to-lerobot-v3_0.

parameters.name: contract
parameters.description: Path, inside the invocation dataset, to the contract YAML that defines which Roboto topics to read and how they map to LeRobot state, action, and video features — see https://docs.roboto.ai/reference/roboto-to-lerobot-contract.html for the contract schema. Defaults to 'contract.yaml' at the dataset root; the run fails if no contract.yaml is found there and this parameter is not set, or if a specified path does not exist in the dataset.

parameters.name: pool_size
parameters.description: Number of worker processes used to read and process events in parallel, per shard. Leave unset to auto-size from the host CPU count: min(16, cpu_count / shard_count) — on the default 16-vCPU compute with shard_count=3 that is 5. Any explicit value is used verbatim and is not capped.

parameters.name: encoder_threads
parameters.description: Level-of-parallelism given to the SVT-AV1 video encoder per camera stream. Must be >= 2: lower values risk the encoder's internal frame queue overflowing under bursty writes, which silently drops frames from the output video. Leave unset to use the built-in value of 2. Only the v3_0 variant acts on it — the v2_1 variant (lerobot 0.3.3) accepts this parameter and silently ignores it, since lerobot 0.3.x has no equivalent encoder-tuning knob, so leave it unset on v2_1.

parameters.name: shard_count
parameters.description: Number of parallel writer shards; each shard independently writes a partial dataset that is then merged (stream-copy, no re-encoding) into the final output. Sharded writing needs a merge API that lerobot 0.3.x lacks, so without episode_cache only the v3_0 variant acts on it: the v2_1 variant (lerobot 0.3.3) accepts this parameter and ignores it, falling back to a single writer and logging a warning. With episode_cache, both variants use it as the maximum number of processes that convert the episodes missing from the cache. Without episode_cache, sharding also changes episode order: episodes in the merged dataset are grouped by shard rather than strictly chronological, though each episode's original start_time_ns is preserved in the output manifest.

parameters.name: episode_cache
parameters.description: Set to 'true' to cache each converted episode in the org's assets, so a re-export converts only new or changed events or sessions. Caching requires org asset storage to be enabled for your org; where it is not enabled, this parameter has no effect: the action logs a warning and converts every event. Each episode is stored once, as a one-episode LeRobot dataset in '.lerobot-cache/', a hidden folder in the org's assets, keyed by the contract, the converter source, the lerobot version, the event or session and its source topics. At most shard_count processes convert the episodes missing from the cache, on both variants, and each new entry is uploaded as soon as it is converted. The export then merges cached and new episodes, always in chronological order, and records which episodes came from the cache in the dataset's lineage file, meta/roboto_lineage.json. Leave unset or 'false' to convert every event without the cache. Both variants act on it, each caching episodes in its own LeRobot format (v2.1 or v3.0).

parameters.name: output_format
parameters.description: What the export writes into the invocation's folder: 'lerobot' (default) writes the LeRobot dataset to combined/; 'lance' writes its Lance layout to lance/ instead; 'both' writes both. After the LeRobot dataset is built, the converter from the lerobot-lancedb package (which LeRobot's lancedb-convert extra installs) writes the Lance layout, with the same videos, metadata and lineage; it converts the whole dataset on every run, even when the episode cache supplied every episode. The Lance layout is read-only and needs LeRobot >= 0.7.0 to read; training can read it in place from object storage with random access instead of downloading the dataset first, though not from Roboto itself, whose read-only dataset credentials do not allow the listing the Lance reader needs: download lance/ or copy it to a bucket you control. LeRobot's tools cannot edit it, merge it or push it to the Hugging Face Hub; keep the LeRobot dataset ('both') for those. Only roboto-to-lerobot-v3_0 supports 'lance' and 'both'; roboto-to-lerobot-v2_1 fails the run before converting.
